detail:
The National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI) describes iron-deficiency anemia as a type of anemia that develops if a person does not have enough iron in the body, and as the most common type of anemia. The body needs iron to make hemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen, so low iron leads to fewer or smaller healthy red blood cells. Causes and risk factors NHLBI lists can include blood loss, not getting enough iron, problems absorbing iron, and periods of higher need such as pregnancy or growth.

People with mild or moderate iron-deficiency anemia may have no symptoms, NHLBI notes. More serious cases can include tiredness, shortness of breath, chest pain, pale skin, headache, and cold hands or feet among the common anemia symptoms sources describe. To diagnose it, clinicians usually order blood tests including a complete blood count, hemoglobin, blood iron levels, and ferritin levels, and then evaluate why iron is low rather than treating the blood result alone.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about iron deficiency anemia symptoms and diagnosis.
